body:
Step B1 of the multi-account design (, sections 2, 3 and the protocol floor in
section 1). Invisible to the user: an upgraded install behaves exactly as before, with one
account row under everything.

## Data

* `accounts` table and `lists.accountId` as in section 2; Room schema 9 with the migration
  described there (one row from `SessionStore` + `ServerConfig`, all lists tagged, token re-keyed
  by local account id, `signedIn` = token present). Migration test in `AppDbMigrationTest.kt`
  style (driver-path workaround), covering: signed-in install, signed-out-with-unpushed-rows
  install (`mirrorAccountId` only), fresh install.
* `SessionStore` becomes `SecretStore`: token per local account id. `ServerConfig.serverUrl`,
  `allowSelfSignedCerts`, `KEY_SYNC_CURSOR`, `KEY_DEFAULT_CURRENCY`, `KEY_IGNORED_INVITE_IDS`,
  `KEY_MIRROR_ACCOUNT_ID` are deleted after migration; `deviceId` stays global.

## Runtime

* `AccountRegistry` (Flow of accounts; add/remove/update; sole writer).
* `AccountSession` per server account: Retrofit/OkHttp client for its base URL with the auth,
  protocol and error interceptors bound to **that** account; per-account `SyncStatus` and cursor.
  401 → `signedIn=false` on that row; 426 → `outdated=true`; a 2xx clears `outdated`. The
  process-wide `SessionEvents` goes away.
* `SyncEngine.syncNow()` iterates signed-in, non-outdated server accounts; per-account failures
  are isolated; the aggregate status is worst-of. `seedStatus()` per account. 410 re-base and
  `deleteSyncedRows()` scoped to one account's lists.
* `ListsRepo.create(accountId, …)`; everything by list id unchanged. `ItemsRepo` unchanged in
  signature.
* `AuthRepository.login/register(serverUrl, …)` creates or re-activates an account row instead
  of writing the single session; `logout(accountId)` keeps unpushed rows and sets
  `signedIn=false` (T-257 semantics per account); `removeAccount(accountId)` deletes its lists,
  items, token and row.
* `UpdateChecker` queries every server account; `PendingInviteHolder` and
  `CollaboratorChangeNotifier` carry the account id.
* View models keep working single-account: they read "the first account" through a small
  `CurrentAccount` shim that B2 removes. Every screen test must still pass.

## Protocol floor

* `MIN_SERVER_PROTOCOL = 3` next to `PROTOCOL_VERSION` in `Protocol.kt`. Before the first
  `/login` or `/register` to a server, `GET /app-version`; refuse with a new local message
  ("This server is too old for this app") when `protocol` is missing or below the floor. Store
  `serverProtocol` on the row; refresh it on every update check. The T-287 rule holds: the
  request goes only to the URL the user confirmed.
* AGENTS.md "Protocol version" bullet gets: *The client must keep working against servers down
  to `MIN_SERVER_PROTOCOL`; a feature that needs a newer server is gated per account by
  `serverProtocol`, never assumed. Raise the floor only in a major release and record it in the
  wire-contract changelog.* `docs/wire-contract.md` protocol section says the same from the
  server's side (no wire change).

## Tests

* Registry, session cache, per-account 401/426 isolation, two-account sync where one server
  fails, migration cases above, floor check (missing `protocol`, below, equal), logout keeps
  unpushed rows for only that account. Each must fail when its change is reverted.
title: Android: multi-account data layer, accounts table, per-account sessions, server protocol floor (B1)
